liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Ripple** (6 reviews): Ripple was the first in eight years; fans who left after the usual closer missed it; A teenage attendee sensed something special was happening when Ripple was pulled out [19][20][24][27][28][30]
- **Let The Good Times Roll** (1 review): Soulful, warm opener, slightly slow; Bobby and Jerry lock together in a series of notes around 6:13 [23]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Jerry barely manages the vocal but hits lovely notes; Brent noodles around 3:45; it fades after about seven minutes [23]
- **Victim Or The Crime** (1 review): Victim Or The Crime gets a somewhat unusual rendition worth hearing [29]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Eyes Of The World is missing an entire verse [28]
- **Drums** (1 review): Billy and Mickey played beach-themed percussion during Drums, which the reviewer says happened only this night, evoking a tropical island [22]

## Setlist highlights

- **1 LPCM Surround Sound Mix (48k)**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [31]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-09-03.136755.5-1.tobin.flac1648** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 142 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1988-09-03.157832.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac1644**: soundboard; 20 songs; 143 min [2]
- **gd1988-09-03.136753.dts.tobin.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 142 min [4]
- **gd1988-09-03.136752.mtx.tobin.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 142 min [5]
- **gd88-09-03.aud.miller.5913.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 139 min; rated 3.67/5 by 15 [12]. Said about its sound: The audience recording's sound quality is only so-so at best; The audience recording has a weird mix [24][29]

## Around the show

- Some people left during One More Saturday Night and later learned they had missed Ripple [19]
- Someone passed the reviewer a Dixie cup during the first set, which the reviewer jokingly blames for the experience [22]
- The reviewer describes the Capital Centre in suburban Maryland as a venue since torn down [23]
- Reviewer says Jerry flubbed lyrics in nearly every song, making the show mediocre [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-09-03.136755.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: flac16/48kHz ; 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound (48k) - SBD (original shnid = 27749)verified SBD> Cassette Master> Dat (SV3800/48k), plus AUD patch; [1]. Also: 5.1 LPCM surround mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC on 20 August 2016 by Trader Little Helper [1]
- **gd1988-09-03.157832.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac1644**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  August 23, 2022; source: Ultramatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [2]
- **gd1988-09-03.136753.dts.tobin.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: DTS-Audio-CD 5.1 Mix ; SBD (original shnid = 27749)verified SBD> Cassette Master> Dat (SV3800/48k), plus AUD patch; [4]. Also: DTS surround mix by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC on 20 August 2016 by Trader Little Helper [4]
- **gd1988-09-03.136752.mtx.tobin.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: Matrix 2 Source Mix - SBD (original shnid = 27749)verified SBD> Cassette Master> Dat (SV3800/48k), plus AUD patch; [5]. Also: Two-source matrix of soundboard and audience, mixed by an archive.org user, FLAC conversion 20 August 2016 by Trader Little Helper [5]
- **gd88-09-03.aud.miller.5913.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by DES and Charlie Miller; source: Audience: Unknown Mics [12]

## Art and photos

- Poster by D.King Gallery: [Grateful Dead 9/3/1988 Washington DC Backstage Pass](https://www.dking-gallery.com/store/Dead_Pass_880903.html) [32]
